content.title: Pop - Definition, Meaning & Synonyms
content.text: Other forms: popped; popping; pops Definitions of pop verb make a sharp explosive noise “The cork of the champagne bottle popped” see moresee less type of: go, soundmake a certain noise or sound verb cause to make a sharp explosive sound “He popped the champagne bottle” verb burst open with a sharp, explosive sound “The balloon popped” “This popcorn pops quickly in the microwave oven” verb cause to burst with a loud, explosive sound “The child popped the balloon” verb fire a weapon with a loud explosive noise “The soldiers were popping” noun a sharp explosive sound as from a gunshot or drawing a cork see moresee less type of: soundthe sudden occurrence of an audible event adverb like a pop or with a pop verb appear suddenly or unexpectedly “The farm popped into view as we turned the corner” “He suddenly popped up out of nowhere” verb put or thrust suddenly and forcefully “pop the pizza into the microwave oven” “He popped the petit-four into his mouth” “He popped me on the head” see moresee less type of: hitdeal a blow to, either with the hand or with an instrument “He popped out to shortstop” see moresee less type of: hitcause to move by striking verb take drugs, especially orally noun an informal term for a father; probably derived from baby talk noun a sweet drink containing carbonated water and flavoring see moresee less type of: soft drinknonalcoholic beverage (usually carbonated) adjective (of music or art) new and of general appeal (especially among young people) noun music of general appeal to teenagers; a bland watered-down version of rock'n'roll with more rhythm and harmony and an emphasis on romantic love "Pop."
